Tom — thanks, quick starter checklist attached and a lean network diagram (see attachments). High level here in the body so your infra reviewers can scan:  

1) VPC & Peering
 - Ensure a dedicated VPC for Redwood Private control/data plane traffic.
 - Create a VPC peering (or cloud interconnect) between GFH-VPC and Redwood-enclave-VPC in the same region.
 - Confirm routing tables include the peered CIDR ranges for both control and data subnets.

2) Subnets & IPs
 - Reserve static/private IPs for the Redwood gateway and NAT instances.
 - Ensure /27 minimum for control-plane subnets to allow for autoscaling.

3) Outbound NAT
 - Outbound token-exchange and image pulls must go through your NAT path.
 - Validate egress rules allow TLS (443) to our registry and telemetry endpoints IP ranges (attached list).

4) Firewall / Security Groups
 - Allow inbound from Redwood control-plane CIDRs on the management port (TCP 8443) for orchestration only.
 - Data-plane ports: 50051 (gRPC) and 443 (HTTPS) between peered subnets.
 - Close SSH from public internet; use bastion/jump-hosts we approve.

5) Service Accounts & Keys
 - Pre-provision a service account with least-privilege for image pull, logging, and KMS decrypt.
 - Provide the service account email and KMS key ARN (if using customer-managed keys).

6) DNS & Certificates
 - If you will use private DNS, add records for our internal gateway FQNs.
 - Share cert signing details if using your CA; Redwood can accept signed certs or use a short-lived cert from our issuance flow.

7) Audit & Logging
 - Enable flow logs for the peered subnets for the validation window.
 - Make sure your SIEM whitelists Redwood telemetry IPs.

Action items for GFH (quick):
 - Create peering and provide peering ID + route table screenshots.
 - Send service account + KMS key identifiers.
 - Provide firewall rule export (JSON or CSV).

Attachments: redwood-enclave-peering-checklist_v1.xlsx (checklist), network-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram), telemetry-ip-list.txt

I also added Marissa to loop in our private-deploy operations checklist and to set up a short validation call. If helpful I can include the small preflight runbook we use for NAT & egress smoke tests.

Tom — quick notes from a security lens (pulling from our SOC playbook):

- KMS: If you require HSM-backed keys, let us know early; CMK rotation windows need coordination.
- Egress allowlist: we'll provide a bundled IP + FQDN list. Prefer FQDNs for cloud-managed ranges where IPs change.
- Traffic inspection: if you have TLS interception, we recommend a short-lived inbound trust (mutual TLS) rather than permanent cert installs.
- Audit evidence: for the acceptance gate, we'll need screenshots of: routing tables, peering status, VPC flow logs enabled, and a successful egress curl to our telemetry endpoint from a host in your control subnet.

I'll include two small test commands in the preflight doc (curl + grpc-healthcheck) so your infra can validate quickly.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
